title: Brussels Sprouts on Buttered Toast
description: Eliza Acton's "Belgian mode" of serving Brussels sprouts: boiled briefly, piled on thick buttered toast, with melted-butter sauce on the side. Her 1845 Modern Cookery was among the first English cookbooks to list ingredients and cooking times, an idea Mrs Beeton later borrowed.
notes:
BRUSSELS SPROUTS.

These delicate little sprouts, or miniature cabbages, should be gathered when not larger than a common walnut, and after being trimmed free from any decayed leaves, and washed very thoroughly, should be thrown into a pan of water properly salted, and boiled from eight to ten minutes, then well drained, and served upon a rather thick round of toasted bread, buttered on both sides. Rich melted butter must be sent to table with them. This is the Belgian mode of dressing this excellent vegetable, which is served in France with the sauce poured over it, or it is tossed in a stewpan with a slice of butter and some pepper and salt: a spoonful or two of veal gravy (and sometimes a little lemon-juice) is added when these are perfectly mixed.

8 to 10 minutes.

Eliza Acton, *Modern Cookery, in all its Branches* (London: Longman, 1845), Chapter XV (Vegetables), p. 331. OCR fixes: "Eich" corrected to "Rich"; words hyphenated across line breaks (vege-table, pep-per) rejoined.

Adapted: Acton's "melted butter", a butter sauce lightly thickened with flour, is given as a short recipe, and the French variation is kept as an optional last step.
ingredients: 1 tablespoon kosher salt, for the cooking water
4 tablespoons (56 g) cold unsalted butter, cubed
steps: Trim the stems of the sprouts and pull off any discoloured outer leaves. Wash well.
Bring a large pan of water to a rolling boil with the salt. Add the sprouts and boil fast, uncovered, until just tender, 8 to 10 minutes. Drain very well.
While the sprouts cook, butter the bread on both sides and toast in a dry skillet over medium heat until golden, 2 to 3 minutes per side.
Melt 1 tablespoon of the butter in a small saucepan over low heat, whisk in the flour, then the water and salt. Simmer for 1 minute, whisking.
Take the pan off the heat and whisk in the rest of the butter a piece at a time until smooth and glossy.
Lay the toast on a warm platter, pile the sprouts on top, and serve the sauce alongside.
For the French way, toss the drained sprouts in a pan with a knob of butter, salt, pepper, a spoonful or two of stock, and a squeeze of lemon.
